edges.description: Foveal cone dysfunction produces a small central scotoma.

A minority of GNAT2 families diverge from the stationary majority into a slowly progressive cone (or cone-rod) dystrophy; this edge marks that minority trajectory rather than the stationary norm of the parent node.
Poor cone ERG from 3 weeks becoming undetectable by 9 months, with cones surviving early.
edges.limitations: cpfl3 is a hypomorphic missense allele rather than a null, the mouse has no fovea, and rod-mediated responses also decline with age, so it is not a pure cone-stationary model.

evidence.snippet: Achromatopsia is characterized by reduced visual acuity, pendular nystagmus, increased sensitivity to light (photophobia), a small central scotoma, eccentric fixation, and reduced or complete loss of color discrimination.

evidence.reference_title: Cone dystrophy phenotype associated with a frameshift mutation (M280fsX291) in the alpha-subunit of cone specific transducin (GNAT2).
evidence.snippet: All five examined patients had a history of nystagmus from infancy, photophobia, defective colour vision, and poor visual acuity.

nodes.description: Although most GNAT2 disease is stationary achromatopsia, an infantile-onset cone dystrophy with slow visual-acuity deterioration is documented.

evidence.reference_title: Cone dystrophy phenotype associated with a frameshift mutation (M280fsX291) in the alpha-subunit of cone specific transducin (GNAT2).
evidence.snippet: Mutation in the alpha-subunit of cone specific transducin (GNAT2) is characterised by an infantile onset cone dystrophy.

nodes.description: The characteristic clinical outcome: congenital, largely stationary cone dysfunction with poor visual acuity, nystagmus, photophobia and loss of colour discrimination in all axes, with preserved scotopic (rod) vision. A minority of GNAT2 families instead show a slowly progressive cone dystrophy.

evidence.snippet: In the complete form of ACHM, affected individuals typically present early in life with nystagmus, photophobia, low visual acuity, and total color blindness.
The cone mosaic in GNAT2-ACHM is relatively well preserved, potentially allowing for a wide therapeutic window for cone-directed interventions.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of cone function without degeneration in a novel Gnat2 knock-out mouse.
evidence.snippet: loss of Gnat2 expression abolished cone phototransduction, yet there was no loss of cones, disruption of the photoreceptor mosaic, nor change in general retinal morphology up to at least 9 months of age.

nodes.description: With transducin unable to relay the signal from opsin to PDE6, the cone cannot generate a light response. Cone-driven (photopic) ERG responses are absent while rod-driven (scotopic) responses are preserved, the electrophysiological signature of a cone-autonomous cascade defect.

evidence.snippet: Our results demonstrate that GNAT2 is the third gene implicated in achromatopsia.

nodes.description: Biallelic GNAT2 variants (typically protein-truncating) abolish the cone photoreceptor-specific alpha subunit of transducin. Cone transducin is the G protein that couples photoactivated cone opsin to cone PDE6, so its loss is the initiating, cone-autonomous lesion in the phototransduction cascade.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the cone photoreceptor G-protein alpha-subunit gene GNAT2 in patients with achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: GNAT2 encodes the cone photoreceptor-specific alpha-subunit of transducin, a G-protein of the phototransduction cascade, which couples to the visual pigment(s).
The mechanism of pathogenicity appears to be biallelic loss-of-function.

nodes.description: The spontaneous cpfl3 missense mouse is the classic GNAT2 achromatopsia model and the model used for the AAV cone rescue; it recapitulates cone functional loss with relatively preserved cones early on.
Frameshift allele identified in a consanguineous family with cone dystrophy / ACHM4.

evidence.reference_title: Mapping of a novel locus for achromatopsia (ACHM4) to 1p and identification of a germline mutation in the alpha subunit of cone transducin (GNAT2).
evidence.snippet: Direct sequence analysis of the candidate gene GNAT2 located within this interval identified a frameshift mutation in exon 7 (c842_843insTCAG; M280fsX291) that segregated with the disease.
